subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: Should an explicit `gateway.bind: "tailnet"` fail gateway startup when no Tailnet IPv4 is available, or is loopback fallback an intentional supported compatibility behavior?
rationale: The current fallback and published explicit-bind documentation conflict, and choosing fail-closed behavior can alter startup behavior for existing installations; the permanent security and upgrade contract requires gateway-owner intent.

options.title: Fail closed for tailnet
options.body: Reject startup with an actionable error when no Tailnet IPv4 is available, matching the documented explicit-bind contract and avoiding silent policy downgrade.

options.title: Preserve fallback explicitly
options.body: Keep loopback fallback but document it as supported behavior, emit a prominent warning, and prove that the resulting authentication policy is intentional and safe.

options.title: Add an explicit compatibility mode
options.body: Make fail-closed behavior canonical while offering a narrowly justified compatibility mechanism only if shipped-user evidence demonstrates a real need.

recommendation.title: Fail closed for tailnet
recommendation.body: Reject startup with an actionable error when no Tailnet IPv4 is available, matching the documented explicit-bind contract and avoiding silent policy downgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: The available discussion and adjacent gateway/Tailscale history make steipete the strongest routing candidate for the listener security contract.
